liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Why Don't We Do it in the Road** (1 review): The band sounds excellent on the opening number [13]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer says Jack Straw soars [21]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Cassidy is jammy in a good way, according to the reviewer [21]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): The opening portion of Terrapin Station is missing from this copy [20]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Garcia repeatedly forgot the lyrics during this song, and his voice cracked [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Why Don't We Do it in the Road**: rare: 7 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd85-04-13.sbd.popi.6146.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 138 min; rated 4.38/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is outstanding, with only an occasional brief glitch; Sound is good for 1985, though static occasionally jolts the listener; The first few seconds of Terrapin Station are cut from this copy; otherwise it sounds fine [12][13][14]
- **gd1985-04-13.178985.senn815.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 18 songs; 136 min [4]
- **gd1985-04-13.senn421.mccue.ford.32595.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 18 songs; 134 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Uploader calls the Sennheiser 421 audience recording's sound quality spectacular [6]
- **gd1985-04-13.fix-shnid-77348.tetzeli.83071.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 135 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [7]. Said about its sound: Uploader calls the McCue audience source excellent and worth hearing for its own sake [7]

## Around the show

- Irvine Meadows had a hard-edged, loud, vocal crowd, rowdier than Bay Area audiences, per this listener [11]
- Garcia's voice and memory were poor, but his guitar playing compensated, according to this listener [17]
- Reviewer watched from the lawn and recalls problematic crowd behavior alongside the high-intensity show [18]
- Parking lot scene was classic; reviewer's friend, new to the band, became a Deadhead that night [19]
- Taper draped the microphones with a black shawl all show to avoid security [6]
- Reviewer thinks the second-set song list is hard to beat for the 1985 period [12]
- Reviewer ranks 1985 among the best-sounding years of the band's career, with Phil especially strong [17]
- Reviewer found the show a little short by the standards of the time [18]
- Energy at LA shows from 1984 to 1988 was unreal, per the reviewer [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-04-13.sbd.popi.6146.sbeok.shnf**: source: sbd> mc> reel> dats> wav> shn [1]. Also: Soundboard copy via Michael Grossman's DAT, transferred by popi through reel and DAT to WAV and shn [1]
- **gd1985-04-13.178985.senn815.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 815 mics > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [4]. Also: Patches: ten seconds of crowd and Peggy-O start from Nakamichi 100 source; fifteen seconds in Drums from Sennheiser 421 source [4]
- **gd1985-04-13.senn421.mccue.ford.32595.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Mark McCue; transferred by Alex Ford; source: MAC: (FOB) Sennheiser 421's* > Sony D5 > Maxell XLII-S 90(Set I) & Maxell MX 90(Set II) [6]. Also: Terrapin Station could not be patched because the only other source is also missing its first seconds [6]
- **gd1985-04-13.fix-shnid-77348.tetzeli.83071.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: Patch fix of shnid 77348 see info file [7]. Also: About a minute of missing drums was patched in from the McCue audience source, matching pitch with crossfades [7]
